When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **3**/10: WARNING but contained vs VIX Spike Tier **4**/4: EXTREME with skew, backwardation, and adaptive all active
Price has not broken yet; the options market is buying protection ahead of a move that is still developing. Trust the VIX Spike: backwardation means the market pays more for near-term vol than deferred, a pricing pattern that precedes dislocation rather than mere nervousness. The crash score will catch up if price confirms.
⚠ These two disagree: Contrarian score **57**: ACCUMULATE partial signal vs Divergence composite TOPPING with **28** bearish pairs vs **4** bullish, **74.4%** of pairs diverging
A partial accumulate read at **57** is a half-sized signal, not a conviction buy. When three-quarters of cross-asset pairs are diverging bearishly, sentiment has not reached the capitulation level that makes contrarian accumulation durable. Use the divergence composite for direction, the contrarian score only for sizing.

Positioning follows the concentration regime at 55% confidence: hold the leaders and cut the laggards without sentiment. USMV versus SPY drifting from -0.93 to +0.00 correlation says low-volatility equity is beginning to decouple from the broad market, which is what happens when capital rotates toward protection. The main risk is a confluence trigger. VIX backwardation is already confirmed active; credit, small-caps, and yen are the three missing legs. The KRE/XLF pair drifting from +0.21 to -0.68 is the early signal to watch: regional banks breaking from broader financials is how credit stress announces itself before spreads move in the public data. If HYG rolls and the T1 times HYG confluence fires, this environment moves from surveillance to defensive immediately.

Macro Regime — where are we structurally
AI read · macro regime

The macro regime is CONCENTRATION at 55% confidence: the market is rewarding a narrow pocket of assets while the rest underperform. A confidence reading of 55% is modest, meaning the concentration signal is real but not yet self-reinforcing.

The regime state scores 60 with a TRANSITION label and MIXED bias. In practice, you hold the leaders (NDX at +0.7% confirms US tech as the current concentration vehicle) and cut laggards without waiting for mean reversion.

A regime score above 65 or confidence above 65% would be the threshold to size the concentration trade with conviction rather than caution.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means assets that normally move together have started moving apart. Correlation drift is simply the shift in that relationship over time: a pair that moves from a correlation of +0.75 to -0.70 has gone from tracking each other closely to moving in opposite directions.

The divergence composite scores a maximum 100 on the DIVERGENCE COMPOSITE label, with 74.4% of the 43 tracked pairs currently pulling in opposite directions and a net bias of 24 bearish pairs above bullish. Six pairs show DEEP DIVERGENCE at score 80 each: the MOVE bond-volatility index, AUD/JPY, V versus MA, NVDA versus AMD, KRE versus XLF, and USMV versus SPY.

The AUD/JPY drift from +0.37 to -0.16 says the yen carry is beginning to unwind as a safe-haven bid builds underneath. The KRE/XLF drift from +0.21 to -0.68 means regional banks are breaking from the broader financial sector, which is how credit stress surfaces before spreads widen officially.

A TOPPING composite at this breadth of divergence is a late-cycle signature.

Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

The Nikkei leads every region at +5.3% over five days while Shanghai sits at -2.8%, a split within Asia that says Japanese equities are absorbing flows that China is repelling. Europe has no safe corner: the DAX leads the region at just -1.3% while the CAC lags at -3.0%.

In the US, NDX holds +0.7% while the Dow sits at -1.3%, a spread that confirms the concentration regime in real time. Crypto offers no diversification: BTC is flat at 0.0% and SOL sheds -2.8%.

The pattern across all four regions is the same: one narrow leadership pocket, broad selling everywhere else. For the US session, the question is whether NDX can extend that slim lead or whether the week's selling in Dow components, Europe, and crypto bleeds into the open.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 3/10 · WARNING — 3+ signals, active surveillance
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The Crash Index at 3/10 and VIX Spike at Tier 4/4 are measuring different things, and their divergence is coherent, not a contradiction. The crash index counts discrete warning flags across price, breadth, and credit.

At 3, enough is flagged to require active surveillance but the threshold for a systemic alert is not cleared. The VIX detector reads the options market's current appetite for near-term insurance: skew active, backwardation active, and adaptive active means dealers and funds are buying protection against a move the price tape has not yet delivered.

The options market is leading price here. If the crash score climbs toward 5 or 6, the VIX positioning will look prescient.

You watch the crash score for confirmation, not reassurance.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 3/10 — a few early signals are stirring; watch whether more line up.

How to read
Heat ranking: composite of RS (relative strength vs SPY), Momentum (price action 20-60d), Breadth (% stocks above SMA), Options flow, and Attention. Use top-5 as rotation focus.
Emerging industries: high velocity = screener scores accelerating this week vs prior baseline — potential early rotation signal.
Competitor themes: token frequency × recency across top finance Substacks — useful narrative context, not a trading signal.
Best R/R: only entries with an active screener leg (PULLBACK / BOTTOM / SMART_MONEY_SURGE etc.). EV% = probabilistic edge per trade. Cross-check with weekly chart before sizing.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
